newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mobil sees its '97 Nigeria output peak 600,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Mobil sees its '97 Nigeria output peak 600,000 bpd.

text.p: Mobil Corp expected its Nigerian oil production to peak at 600,000 barrels per day (bpd) in 1997 and increase to 900,000 bpd by the end of the century, a senior Mobil official said.
Mobil currently pumps about 450,000 bpd from its Nigerian fields.

Stephen Wyman, vice president, international negotiator centre, Mobil new exploration and producing ventures, said at a sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals conference on Wednesday that Nigeria has been an important base for Mobil since it began operations by selling kerosene 90 years ago.
"Our explorationists there have discovered 37 offshore fields and 18 of them are currently producing through nine production platforms.
"We expect our total production to reach 600,000 barrels a day this year and 900,000 around the turn of the century," Wyman said.
He said Mobil's upstream company along with its partner, the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation, had to date produced more than two billion barrels of crude oil and condensate.
Nigeria, a member of OPEC, currently produces a total of about 2.15 million bpd of oil with reserves put at 22 billion barrels.
Wyman said Mobil had dramatic success in its newest Africa affiliate, Equatorial Guinea.
The Zafiro field had been brought to production within 18 months of its discovery -- which was faster than any similar-sized project in the history of the oil industry.
"Production at 7,000 barrels a day began in August 1996 and currently stands at 40,000 barrels. Next year the field will reach full production of 80,000 barrels a day".
He said through additional drilling, Mobil had found an extension to the Zafiro field and discovered two satellite fields.
"It's too early to say exactly where all this will yield, except that wherever it leads will be economic progress for the people of Equatorial Guinea," he said.
In Angola, Mobil is working to strengthen the country as an oil and gas producer.
"We're evaluating the commerciality of a deepwater block we operate in the lightly explored Kwanza basin and we have an interest in an offshore block in Angola's Congo basin".
